title: Missed ITR Filing? Options for Previous Years Explained
description: If you missed filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) for previous years, you might still have options to rectify the situation. The primary avenue for most taxpa.

faq.a: An Updated Return allows taxpayers to correct omissions or errors in their previously filed or unfiled ITRs. It enables declaration of undisclosed income within two years from the end of the relevant assessment year, by paying additional tax.

faq.q: Can I file an Updated Return to claim a refund?
faq.a: No, an Updated Return (ITR-U) cannot be filed if it results in a refund, an increase in a refund, or a decrease in your total tax liability. It is specifically for increasing tax liability or reducing a loss.

Condonation of Delay is a special provision under Section 119(2)(b) of the Income Tax Act, allowing the CBDT to accept applications for claims (like refunds or deductions) even after the prescribed deadline, typically in cases of genuine hardship.

faq.q: What are the penalties for not filing ITR on time?
faq.a: If your total income exceeds ₹5 lakhs, a late filing fee of ₹5,000 is levied under Section 234F. For income up to ₹5 lakhs, the fee is ₹1,000. Additionally, interest under Section 234A, 234B, and 234C may apply on unpaid tax.

faq.q: When is the deadline for filing an Updated Return?
faq.a: An Updated Return can be filed within two years from the end of the relevant assessment year. For example, for AY 2022-23 (FY 2021-22), the deadline for ITR-U is March 31, 2025.

faq.q: Can I carry forward losses if I file an ITR-U?
faq.a: If you missed filing your original return, you generally lose the ability to carry forward most types of losses (e.g., capital losses, business losses) to future years. Filing an ITR-U does not retroactively restore this benefit for a year where the original return was not filed on time.
